rotation.spin: OPPOSITE arms spin the SAME way: FRONT+BACK = CW pair; RIGHT+LEFT = CCW pair. This is the PLUS-style pairing, and it is a deliberate correction of the source tutorial's 'Front+Right CW, Back+Left CCW' (that is the X-configuration rule wrongly applied to a plus layout — with it, every pitch correction would also yaw the drone).
rotation.prop: Prop always follows its motor: CW prop on a CW motor, CCW prop on a CCW motor. mosfetChannel.leadA: RED (+) lead -> board pad M1+, which sits ON the BAT+ rail
mosfetChannel.leadB: BLUE (-) lead -> board pad M1-, which is the DRAIN node. (CCW motors use WHITE (+) / BLACK (-) instead of red/blue.)

mosfetChannel.component: 1N5819 Schottky flyback diode D1 (DO-41 axial, 1 A / 40 V) — sits across the motor
mosfetChannel.leadA: CATHODE = the end with the printed BAND -> M1+ / the BAT+ rail (the motor's '+' side). THE BAND POINTS AT BAT+.
mosfetChannel.leadB: ANODE = the plain unbanded end -> M1- / the Drain node (the motor's '-' side). Reversed, this diode is a dead short across the battery through the MOSFET the moment the gate goes high — it smokes.

mosfetChannel.component: IRLB8721 Q1 — GATE, the LEFT leg when the printed label faces you and the legs point down
mosfetChannel.leadA: One end of the 100 ohm gate resistor (whose other end is the G1 pad)
mosfetChannel.leadB: One end of the 10 kohm pull-down (whose other end is the GND rail). Both resistors meet AT THE GATE LEG — the 10 k is on the MOSFET side of the 100 ohm, not the GPIO side.

mosfetChannel.component: IRLB8721 Q1 — DRAIN, the MIDDLE leg
mosfetChannel.leadA: M1- pad — i.e. the motor's '-' lead and the diode's anode, all one node
mosfetChannel.leadB: Nothing else. The Drain node terminates here. It is NOT tied to BAT+ and NOT tied to GND.

mosfetChannel.component: IRLB8721 Q1 — the METAL TAB (electrically identical to the Drain)
mosfetChannel.leadA: Internally bonded to Drain — the tab IS the motor's '-' node, live whenever the battery is in
mosfetChannel.leadB: MUST TOUCH NOTHING: heat-shrink over every tab (unconditional), >= 2 empty holes to the next MOSFET, never the BAT+ rail, never the GND rail, never another tab (that would join all four motors into one), never the carbon plate 1 mm away.

mosfetChannel.component: IRLB8721 Q1 — SOURCE, the RIGHT leg
mosfetChannel.leadA: Bent over onto the GND rail
mosfetChannel.leadB: Soldered to the GND rail. This is a LOW-SIDE switch: the motor is always at battery potential; the MOSFET only completes the path to ground.

mosfetChannel.leadA: G1 pad — the pad where the YELLOW 28-30 AWG wire from ESP32 GPIO 25 lands
mosfetChannel.leadB: Q1's Gate leg. Why: the gate is a ~1.5 nF capacitor; 3.3 V / 100 ohm = 33 mA peak for under a microsecond, inside the GPIO's 40 mA rating.

mosfetChannel.leadA: Q1's Gate leg (same node as the 100 ohm's MOSFET-side end)
mosfetChannel.leadB: GND rail. Why: it holds the gate at 0 V during the ~1 s of boot when GPIOs float, during reset, and if the gate wire ever falls off. From the DevKit pin the meter reads ~10 kohm through the 100 ohm — the 9-11 kohm check at M3 and M7.

warnings: ROTATION IS THE #1 THING TO GET WRONG. Plus-style, NOT X-style: FRONT and BACK are the CW pair, RIGHT and LEFT are the CCW pair. The source tutorial's 'Front + Right CW, Back + Left CCW' is explicitly overruled in Arduino_Project_8.md 'Rotation pairs'. If a drawing shows adjacent arms spinning the same way, it is wrong and the firmware mixer (01_flight.ino:331-334) will fight it.

DIODE BAND ORIENTATION. The 1N5819's printed BAND (cathode) faces BAT+ / the motor's '+' side; the plain anode end faces the Drain / motor '-'. Drawn the other way it is a dead short across the LiPo through the MOSFET. On the perfboard layout the band therefore points UP toward the BAT+ rail.
ELECTROLYTIC POLARITY. 220 uF: LONG leg = '+' -> BAT+ rail; the leg beside the printed STRIPE = '-' -> GND rail. Do not draw the stripe on the BAT+ side.

MOSFET LEG ORDER. IRLB8721, printed LABEL FACING THE VIEWER and legs pointing DOWN: G - D - S, left to right. The METAL TAB IS THE DRAIN, not ground — so it is live, it must be heat-shrunk, and two tabs touching joins two motors. A drawing that shows the tab bolted down, grounded, or touching a neighbour or the carbon plate is teaching a short circuit.
LOW-SIDE, NOT HIGH-SIDE. The motor is between BAT+ and the Drain. Never draw the motor between the MOSFET and ground, and never draw the Drain tied to a rail.
10 k PULL-DOWN GOES ON THE MOSFET SIDE OF THE 100 OHM. From the Gate leg to GND, not from the G1 pad to GND. (The meter reads ~10 k either way, which is why it is easy to draw wrong.)

MPU6050 ORIENTATION. Chip side UP, board FLAT to the plate (check by eye from the side), silk-screen X ARROW POINTING AT THE FRONT MOTOR — then the Y arrow points LEFT. A tilted pad or a rotated arrow produces a drone that always leans, and the fix is the mounting, never the code.
DEVKIT ORIENTATION. Micro-USB connector faces the BACK arm. Do not draw the USB toward FRONT.

LEFT/RIGHT HEADER NAMING IS THE BRIEF'S, NOT A VIEW DIRECTION. The brief's 'right header' is the column VIN, GND, 13, 12, 14, 27, 26, 25, 33, 32, 35, 34, VN, VP, EN (USB at the bottom); its 'left header' is 3V3, GND, 15, 2, 4, 16, 17, 5, 18, 19, 21, 3, 1, 22, 23. Because the DevKit is mounted USB-toward-BACK, those columns appear MIRRORED in a top-down drone view. Label every pin by NAME, never by side.

TWO DIFFERENT GND PINS, AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE IN THE DRAWING. The DevKit has exactly one GND per side. GND next to VIN = MT3608 OUT- (power return). GND next to 3V3 = MPU6050 GND. Swapping them in a figure contradicts T1 M5's Stuck note, which students use to diagnose.

5 V GOES TO VIN ONLY. Never draw MT3608 OUT+ into 3V3, and never draw the battery into 3V3 or into VIN directly. Only the ESP32 sees 5.0 V; only the MPU6050 sees 3.3 V; motors see raw battery. There is exactly ONE MT3608 and NO booster on the motor rail.
MOTOR POWER DOES NOT COME FROM THE MT3608. A figure that routes motor current through the boost module is wrong: motors run directly off the 1S cell through their MOSFETs.

THE CARBON PLATES CONDUCT. Every board must be drawn sitting on a visible full-footprint insulating layer (foam tape + a 0.5-1 mm Kapton/plastic shim), never on bare carbon, never on corner dots or a centre dot. The DevKit's 30 protruding pin tips (2-3 mm) must be shown sunk into 3 mm foam or clipped flush. The MOSFET board's solder side never faces bare plate.
BATTERY IS HELD BY O-RINGS ONLY. Never draw a zip tie or tape across the LiPo cell. The bay sits under the bottom plate on a 2 mm foam/EVA pad; the cell must slide out by hand.

PH2.0 POLARITY IS NOT STANDARDISED on micro-drone batteries. Do not draw a plug whose colour order implies a guaranteed polarity; the build step is 'check with the meter, red must read positive'. A reverse-reading battery is retired, never 'just flipped'.

PROPS ARE THE LAST THING FITTED. Any figure of a build, wiring, upload, or bench step must show BARE MOTOR SHAFTS. Props exist in exactly two scenes: the M11 inverted bench thrust test and the M13 tethered flight line. There are NO prop guards in this kit.

THE THRUST RIG IS INVERTED. The drone sits UPSIDE-DOWN on the post with props pointing DOWN at the scale pan, held by two rubber bands across the CENTRE PLATES (never across arms or motors), prop plane >= 65 mm above the pan, post top <= 45 mm across, plus a SLACK 30 cm backup line. The upright rig was explicitly scrapped (it under-reads 30-70 %). Do not draw a drone sitting the right way up on a scale.

TETHER GEOMETRY. The line girth-hitches to the 10 mm cord loop hanging ~10 mm below the BOTTOM plate (under the CG) — the frame has NO 'centre ring'. Anchor is FLAT and <= 10 cm tall, never an upright bottle: the drone hovers at 10-30 cm, inside a standing bottle's height. Lift-off mark ~40 cm from the anchor X so the slack line lies flat and the drone never hovers over the anchor.

WIRE-COLOUR CONFLICT BETWEEN THE BRIEF AND THE EXISTING FIGURES. The brief's canonical pin map says gates = yellow (25) / orange (26) / green (14) / blue (27), SDA = white, SCL = grey. The repo's already-built Fritzing figures (images/fritzing/w_p8_05_signals.json) use orange/orange/green/green for the gates and blue SDA / yellow SCL. New illustrations should follow the BRIEF's pin map, and the discrepancy should be flagged to Yon rather than silently propagated.

MOSFET BOARD SIZE CONFLICT. The brief specifies ~4 x 5 cm (40 x 50 mm) perfboard; the repo's Fritzing part (_fritzing_kit/draw_p8_parts.py board_svg) draws a 70 x 50 mm board despite its own comment saying 50 x 40. Use the brief's 40 x 50 mm.

POWER-TREE TOPOLOGY DETAIL. The brief routes MT3608 IN+/IN- from the MOSFET board's SECOND BAT+/GND pads (the board is the junction). The existing figure w_p8_03_power_tree.json draws lipo.+ straight to mt.Vin — electrically the same node, but a build drawing should show the board's spare pads as the take-off point, because that is what the student solders.

NO FIRMWARE/BRIEF PIN DISAGREEMENT EXISTS. All three sketches (00_motor_test.ino:103-107, 01_flight.ino:145-158, T2_flight_starter.ino:106-112) agree exactly with the brief's pin map: FRONT 25, RIGHT 26, BACK 14, LEFT 27, SDA 21, SCL 22, LED 2. Any figure showing other numbers is wrong regardless of which source it came from.

GPIO 14 TWITCH IS EXPECTED, NOT A FAULT. A <=0.1 s BACK-motor twitch at battery plug-in is normal (GPIO 14 pulses at reset). A motor that KEEPS turning means pull the plug. If a figure annotates power-up behaviour, say this.
A 'FULL DRONE' FIGURE MUST NOT SHOW USB AND BATTERY TOGETHER. USB in = battery out, battery in = USB out. Drawing both cables attached contradicts the rule that carries the whole safety model.

MOTOR-BOARD CHANNEL ORDER ON THE FRAME. M1 pad must be nearest the FRONT arm, and the board carries a marker arrow 'FRONT'. A drawing that lets the board sit any way round loses the one physical cue that stops a channel/arm mismatch.

PROPS-ON EMERGENCY RULE IS A GEOMETRY FACT. The PH2.0 plug exits at the frame's side and sits UNDER the propeller discs — that is why nobody's hand may reach for the plug with props on. If a figure shows the plug, show it under the prop plane so the rule reads as obvious.
SPIN DIRECTION IS 'SEEN FROM ABOVE'. State the viewpoint on every rotation arrow. An isometric view from below silently reverses every arrow.
